findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can create duplicate Bleve indexes
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu during index creation and only locks for the final cache assignment. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource (for example, eager startup indexing racing a Search or watch-event getOrCreateIndex call, or two concurrent lazy builds for a missing key) can both call bleve.New/NewMemOnly, both run the builder, and both write the cache entry. For file-backed indexes they use the same directory, which can fail with lock/already-exists errors or interfere with each other; for all indexes the overwritten index is never closed, leaking its resources and leaving one caller with an index that is no longer the cached/searchable one. The previous whole-build lock serialized this; the finer-grained lock needs per-key deduplication or a check-and-reserve entry under the lock before building.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu while BuildIndex now concurrently inserts into that map at line 138 after releasing most of its work from the lock. searchSupport.init calls TotalDocs after starting the watch goroutine, and later lazy builds can also run concurrently, so this can race with a map write and cause a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic that cannot be recovered. TotalDocs should snapshot the indexes under RLock (or hold RLock while counting) before calling DocCount.

findings.title: NewResourceServer now blocks on full index building and leaks background work on init failure
findings.body: NewResourceServer synchronously calls s.Init(ctx) with the server's background-derived context, so construction now blocks until lifecycle init, full search indexing, and watcher setup finish, and callers cannot cancel or time out that work with their own context. If Init fails part-way (for example after search.init has started its WatchWriteEvents goroutine, which uses context.Background(), or after lifecycle Init), NewResourceServer returns nil and an error without calling s.Stop/s.cancel, leaving the caller no handle to stop the lifecycle backend or background goroutines. Previously lazy Init let server construction succeed and deferred this cost/failure to first use; eager init needs cleanup on failure and a cancellable startup context.

findings.title: Postgres module-server regression is hidden by skipping the test
findings.body: The change adds an unconditional skip for GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres with only a TODO saying the test does not work in Drone. This removes the only integration coverage for running the storage-server target without an HTTP server exactly in the configuration affected by moving unified-storage initialization into server construction, so a postgres-specific startup/init failure can merge and remain undetected. The skip should be tied to a tracked failure/issue or the underlying Drone/postgres init problem should be fixed instead of silently dropping coverage.
